Stirred by a low humming sound, I awoke from my slumber. My eyes opened and I beheld a red glow, not from the soft light of my campfire, but of a large gate, twice the height of a man. Twisting lines of blazing red wound around it, and it bore something like wounds, as though pierced by arrows, but not of flesh.
一阵低沉的嗡鸣将我惊醒。我睁开双眼，看到一片红光，不是营火柔和的光，而是一扇大门，足有两人高。炽红的线条缠绕盘绕其上，门上还有像是伤口的东西，仿佛被箭矢穿透，却不是血肉之躯。

All around it lay solid stone, but in the center I saw something familiar; the place where I had laid among the trees. A strange creature rummaged through my supplies. Its beady eyes jerked towards me, and it hissed. Its skin was green, and it had roughly made armor and a whip at its side.

	It drew its arm back, ready to lash at me, when a shimmer passed over the gate, and the creature perceived me no more.

四周全是坚硬的岩石，但中央却是我熟悉的东西，我曾在林间躺卧的那片地方。一只奇怪的生物正在翻找我的补给。它珠子般的眼睛猛地转向我，发出嘶声。它的皮肤是绿色的，身上披着粗糙的护甲，腰间挂着一条鞭子。

	它抡起手臂，正要向我抽来，这时门上一道微光闪过，那生物再也看不见我了。

Frightened, I backed away, and nearly tumbled over a ledge into a fiery darkness. Flames licked upwards, and strange appendages lashed out as if searching for food.

	Overcome with terror, I fled down a rocky path, deeper into whatever realm I had come to.

	Days passed, and I recalled words my father had taught me. Survival is not always about finding food where there is none, but sometimes about

我吓得连连后退，险些翻下崖沿，坠入一片火光冲天的黑暗。火焰向上翻卷，奇怪的附肢挥来挥去，仿佛在寻觅食物。

	惊恐之下，我沿一条碎石小径奔逃，一路深入这个我误入的领域。

	数日过去，我想起了父亲教过我的话：生存，并不总要在没有食物之处找到食物，有时而在于
res#60479/whatIHaveToSay[3]

going without any at all and still being able to stand. When water is scarce, slow your breath, and do not talk. Every wasted drop is precious.

	I sought for a cool place, but there was none. So I dug. With a jagged rock I dug until I found cool earth, and then lay in it. Above me, strange plants, like lichen, grew amongst the rocks. I pulled them off and covered myself.

……哪怕滴水不沾，也依然能站立起来。当水稀少时，放缓呼吸，不要说话。每一滴浪费的水都弥足珍贵。

	我寻找凉爽的地方，却遍寻不见。于是我挖掘。我用一块锯齿状的石头挖到凉爽的泥土，然后躺了进去。在我上方，奇怪的植物像地衣一样长在岩石之间。我把它们扯下来，盖在身上。

For three days I did and said nothing. I slept when I could, and fretted when I could not sleep.

	This kind of survival could only go on for so long. I had to venture back. I moved the brush, stood, and fear filled my heart. Before me stood... no, flew, a creature unlike any I had ever seen. It hung like a snake caught by an eagle. A halo, with one singular eye, circled its face. And it spoke. I could not understand what it said, for my heart beat so loudly that all else was drowned out.

整整三天，我没有行动，也没有说话。能睡的时候就睡，睡不着时就焦躁不安。

	这样的求生撑不了多久。我必须回去一趟。我拨开灌木，站起身，恐惧攫住了我的心。在我面前站着（不，是飞着）一只我从未见过的生物。它悬停着，像被鹰抓住的蛇。一道光环绕着脸庞旋转，光环上只有一只独眼。它开口说话了。我听不懂它说了什么，因为我的心跳声太响，淹没了一切。

I ran, and when I could run no longer I at last saw the gate I had come through. I cared not if the creature from before still held my camp. I ran though it at full speed, and came at last to rest in the world I knew. The camp was ransacked, but the creature was gone. I looked over my shoulder, but there was no gate. Still, I felt as though something watched me.

	I grabbed my things, and ran home to tell everyone I knew.

我跑啊跑，直到再也跑不动，终于看见了我穿过的那扇门。我不管先前那只怪物是否还占着我的营地，全速冲了过去，终于回到了我熟悉的世界。营地被洗劫一空，但怪物不见了。我回头望去，哪里还有门的影子。可我还是觉得，有什么东西在注视着我。

	我抓起自己的东西，跑回家，把这一切告诉了我认识的每一个人。

Start

What a mistake that was. I was derided as a fool, or a man gone mad. None believe my tale to this day, so I leave this last letter. On my deathbed, I recount, so that perhaps someday, long after my death, I will be known not as a fool, but as a survivor, and a herald of things unseen.


- Maurin Tangelf, the madman of Pirmory.

那真是个天大的错误。人们嘲笑我是个蠢货，或是个发了疯的人。直到今天也没人相信我的故事，所以我留下这最后一封信。临终之际，我把一切重新讲述出来：但愿在很久以后，我不再被当作疯子，而是被记作一名幸存者，一个未曾目睹之物的传信人。


毛林·坦格尔夫，皮尔莫里的疯子。
